newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The administrative court controversy has taken a new twist after the Social Action Party makes a veiled threat it may withdraw from the coalition government if the cabinet decides not to let the Justice Ministry oversee the new court. The party has thrown its support behind the judiciary's bid to take control of the administrative court although Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has openly taken a firm stand that it should be kept under the Council of State. (BANGKOK POST)

- Social Action Party leader Montri Pongpanich has rejected assignments given him by the prime minister in a demonstration of dissent over the Nong Ngu Hao airport conflict. Montri has given PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh a letter saying he will not serve as vice-chairman of the Second Bangkok International Airport committee and chairman of the State Land Encroachment Solution committee. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) has decided to ask the government to stay away from the assembly's mission to gather public opinion on the content of the new charter. CDA President Uthai Pimchaichon was commissioned to ask Prime Minister Chavalit to request that the Campaign for Political Reform Committee stay clear of the CDA's work. (THE NATION) + + + +

- The government's revenue target for the 1997 fiscal year is being adjusted downwards, reducing the previous net revenue target by over 59 billion baht. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has met with officials from the Finance Ministry, the National Economic and Social Development Board and the Bank of Thailand to discuss the budget problem. The meeting has agreed to propose a balanced budget cut to the Cabinet in order to resolve the problem of low revenue collection. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand is ready to step up political pressure on the European Union for the restoration of trade privileges if current efforts fail. Prime Minister Chavalit is poised to raise the issue of Thailand's reduced incentives under the Generalised System of Preferences when he visits Brussels in late April or May. (BANGKOK POST)

- The large first-quarter budget deficit leaves little leeway to relax monetary policy, as previously anticipated as a measure to stimulate business activity. Prominent opposition member of parliament says the latest budget figures are likely to prevent the Bank of Thailand from allowing interest rates to fall much further. (THE NATION)
